checkpoints.name: all_three_transfers_fail
checkpoints.description: The loopback should return each byte unchanged, but every transfer fails — the link is alive (data moves) yet the received bytes are wrong. This is a bring-up, not a finished IP.

checkpoints.name: chip_select_idle
checkpoints.description: In the waveform, chip-select rests high (inactive) before the first transfer begins. Confirms the waveform loads and the master starts from idle.

checkpoints.name: two_shift_registers
checkpoints.description: In NetCrux, the SPI master is built from two shift registers — one for MOSI (transmit), one for MISO (receive). The receive shift register is where the bring-up bug lives.

cross_tool_deep_links.name: failing_test_to_sclk_timing
cross_tool_deep_links.source_action: open a failing loopback result and debug the transfer in the waveform
cross_tool_deep_links.expected_target_state: SCLK, MOSI and MISO are shown; reading the sampled bits against the SCLK edges reveals the receive path captures one SCLK too late — every byte comes back shifted by a bit

cross_tool_deep_links.name: waveform_to_rx_shift_register
cross_tool_deep_links.source_action: from the mis-sampled MISO, cross-probe to the receive datapath
cross_tool_deep_links.expected_target_state: the receive shift register is shown, where the sample-enable timing that causes the one-bit shift can be traced and fixed
